headline: High: shared server datastore and overlapping file/tool surfaces make prompt injection, leakage, and action-cascade risks plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write server files and uses browser/HTTP tools; OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP/REST/FastAPI interfaces. The pair has no documented provenance tracking, so content from Flowise flows could be fed into OpenBBTerminal through shared files or tool outputs and be treated as instructions. This is plausible in default deployments, though not proven.
conditions: IF Flowise flow outputs are copied into OpenBBTerminal prompts or MCP inputs without sanitization
IF both agents share a datastore or filesystem path for intermediate artifacts
mitigations: Add a strict delimiter/template around all inter-agent text
Disable automatic ingestion of file contents into prompts
Route handoffs through a human-reviewed JSON schema
Log and reject any instruction-like text in data fields
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to every cross-agent artifact

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs and secrets, and can write server files; OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data and exposes APIs/MCP. If they share a workspace or datastore, sensitive financial or credential material can move between them. The profiles do not show isolation by default, so leakage is plausible.
conditions: IF both agents access the same server datastore or filesystem
IF Flowise stores tool credentials or chatflow outputs in files readable by OpenBBTerminal
mitigations: Separate workspaces and mount points per agent
Rotate any shared credentials immediately
Restrict OpenBBTerminal to least-privilege data sources
Delete transient artifacts after each run
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls at the storage layer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Flowise has broad network egress and filesystem write, while OpenBBTerminal can connect to MCP/REST/FastAPI services and supports multiple instances. Even without shell or git writes, both can mutate shared external resources or files if deployed together, creating race conditions and inconsistent state. The profiles do not show locking or coordination.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same shared directory or datastore
IF OpenBBTerminal MCP tools and Flowise flows target the same external API or local service
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Disable concurrent runs against the same resource
Review and deduplicate API side effects manually
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is a graph-based agent flow builder that can emit tool outputs, and OpenBBTerminal is a financial-modeling agent with API/MCP access. If OpenBBTerminal consumes Flowise output as authoritative, a mistaken or injected fact can propagate into financial actions or reports. No verification step is documented, so the default cascade risk is high.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal uses Flowise output as a source of truth without independent validation
IF Flowise-generated summaries are forwarded into financial workflows or reports
mitigations: Require source citations before acting on any Flowise output
Add a second-pass verification prompt in OpenBBTerminal
Limit Flowise to drafting only, not decision inputs
Flag low-confidence or uncited claims for manual review
requires-engineering: implement structured validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Flowise handles chatflow inputs/outputs and tool credentials, while OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data. If EU PII, financial records, or licensed datasets are routed through OpenBBTerminal without a matching DPA/residency policy, compliance breach risk is material. The profiles show no aligned retention or residency controls, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF regulated financial or personal data is processed in the shared workflow
IF retention or residency requirements differ between the two deployments
mitigations: Classify data before routing it between agents
Block regulated data from non-approved paths
Document retention and deletion rules for both systems
Confirm DPA/residency coverage for each deployment
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement to the orchestrator
